Just now

I opened my laptop that morning to a support ticket that made my chest go tight. A user was asking, calmly, almost politely, why their account dashboard was showing a balance that was not theirs.
Not a rounding error. Not a stale number. Someone else’s actual money, sitting on their screen, in their name.
Three days earlier I had shipped the fastest version of that dashboard anyone on the team had ever seen. Load time went from four seconds to under fifty milliseconds.
People were congratulating me in the group chat. I remember feeling that particular warmth you get when a graph finally bends the way you wanted it to.
I did not know yet that the same change causing that warmth was also handing strangers each other’s private numbers, one request at a time, without a single error being logged anywhere.
One Line I Was Proud Of
The dashboard endpoint used to hit the database directly on every load. Correct, but slow. So I did the obvious thing and wrapped it in a cache.
cache = {}def get_dashboard_data(user_id):
if "dashboard" in cache:
return cache["dashboard"]
